messages:
maria: Quick question — running into a race on iOS RN (WKWebView) where a streaming fetch gets cut shortly after we rotate the auth token. We postMessage the new token to the webview and then re-create the fetch, but the original ReadableStream aborts ~1-2s after the swap. Anyone seen this?

jay: Yep, seen similar. Safari-based webviews can be aggressive about keep-alive when request headers change. Are you doing SSE or fetch+ReadableStream?

maria: fetch + ReadableStream from the hosted API. We update Authorization header from the native side and then recreate the request in the webview. The UX is fine, but the old stream aborts unexpectedly rather than cleanly closing.

noah: That's expected behavior — a live fetch stream is tied to that TCP/HTTP connection. You can't "swap" auth mid-stream and keep the same response. Two approaches: 1) use short-lived tokens and proactively rotate by opening a new connection before expiry, 2) have the server support resume/offset so client can reconnect and continue where it left off.

olivia: For RN iOS specifically: if you're relying on cookies for refresh, WKWebView requires proper cookie config (SameSite=None; Secure) and sometimes manual cookie syncing. If you're passing Authorization in headers from native -> webview, be aware that creating a new request is the only safe way.

jay: Another pattern is to run a tiny in-webview proxy (worker) that handles token handoff and then opens streams on behalf of the page. ServiceWorkers in WKWebView are hit-or-miss though.

maria: Also seeing intermittent CORS preflight 403 when reconnecting with Authorization header — our OPTIONS sometimes gets 403. CORS config looks like it should allow it though.

noah: Common mistakes: not echoing Access-Control-Allow-Headers properly (need to include Authorization), and returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * while also using credentials. Make sure your OPTIONS handler returns the correct headers early. Example: 

```http
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization,Content-Type
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,OPTIONS
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

olivia: Also check CDNs / proxies — some strip OPTIONS or drop custom headers. If token refresh happens on a different subdomain, ensure the CORS allow list includes it.

jay: For React Native WebView specifics: if you load from file:// or a custom scheme, enable universal access (Android) or use proper originWhitelist. And on iOS, confirm WKWebView config allows _shared_ cookies if you're syncing cookies from native.

maria: Good call. One more: reconnect strategy for streaming — what do we do for UX so it's not a jarring reload?

noah: Exponential backoff with jitter is standard. Add an immediate short retry for transient <2s flaps to avoid churn. If your server supports continuation, include a resume token or message index so the new stream can pick up without re-sending full context. Also proactively refresh tokens before expiry to avoid mid-stream expiration.

ci-bot: FYI — I added a note in #incidents about the recent CORS header tweak on the staging API (https://staging.api.example.com) which might explain some OPTIONS failures. :white_check_mark:

maria: Perfect — plan: (1) enforce re-create stream on token rotation, (2) add resume token support server-side, (3) fix OPTIONS/CORS on CDN, (4) implement backoff+jitter + proactive refresh. Will try the service-worker approach if the UX still stutters. Thanks all :pray:
